skill.name: mirrord-config
skill.description: Helps users generate, edit, and validate mirrord.json configuration files for mirrord (MetalBear). Use when the user wants to connect their local process to a Kubernetes environment, configure features (env/fs/network), or needs feedback on an existing mirrord.json. Always ensures output JSON is valid and schema-conformant.
skill.summary: Generate, validate, and explain least-privilege mirrord configuration files for Kubernetes development workflows.
skill.author: metalbear-co

content.value_statement: Kubernetes configuration files can be difficult to write and easy to misconfigure. This skill creates, validates, and explains focused mirrord configurations.
actual_capabilities: Generate valid mirrord configurations from a stated Kubernetes workflow.
Validate configuration structure against the bundled mirrord schema.
Explain environment, filesystem, network, and target settings.
Fix invalid JSON and unsupported configuration keys.
Identify risky or unnecessary settings and suggest narrower alternatives.
limitations: It does not install mirrord or Kubernetes tools automatically.
It cannot verify cluster access, permissions, or live resource names.
It does not replace testing against the exact mirrord and cluster versions.
It should not receive or reproduce secret values in configuration output.

use_cases.title: Create a Local Development Config
use_cases.description: Describe a target pod, namespace, and required features to receive a minimal configuration for local development.

use_cases.title: Review an Existing Config
use_cases.description: Paste a mirrord configuration to identify schema errors, unnecessary settings, and behavior that may surprise a development team.

use_cases.title: Explain Network and Filesystem Modes
use_cases.description: Ask for a focused explanation of traffic handling, environment mirroring, or remote filesystem behavior before changing a configuration.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: Generate a Minimal Config
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a minimal mirrord configuration for my local service. Target pod API_SERVER in namespace staging. Mirror environment variables only.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: Validate a Config
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this mirrord configuration against the official schema. List errors first, then warnings, then a corrected configuration without adding speculative settings.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: Tune Traffic Handling
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a mirrord configuration for a staging service that mirrors incoming traffic on port 8080 and keeps unrelated traffic unchanged. Explain each setting.

prompt_templates.title: Expert: Reduce Configuration Risk
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this mirrord configuration for unnecessary environment, filesystem, and network access. Propose the smallest change set that preserves the requested workflow.

output_examples.input: Connect a local API process to a staging pod and mirror only selected environment variables.
output_examples.output: A minimal, schema-aligned configuration plan with a pod target, staging namespace, and an explicit environment allowlist.

output_examples.input: My configuration uses local filesystem mode because the application runs local source code.
output_examples.output: An explanation that local source is already handled by mirrord defaults, plus a recommendation to remove the unnecessary filesystem override.

output_examples.input: Validate a configuration with an unsupported option and malformed JSON.
output: A corrected configuration plan using documented keys only.

best_practices: State the target, namespace, and required behavior before generating a configuration.
Prefer minimal settings and validate against the schema before use.
Review environment, filesystem, and network access for least privilege.
anti_patterns: Do not add settings to guess at an unexplained timeout or connection failure.
Do not include credentials, private keys, or full environment values in prompts.
Do not treat a generated configuration as proof of cluster access or runtime compatibility.

faq.question: What is mirrord-config?
faq.answer: It is a skill for generating, validating, fixing, and explaining mirrord configuration files.

faq.question: Can it create a configuration from plain language?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the target, namespace, and features you need, and it will propose a minimal configuration.

faq.question: Does it validate JSON syntax?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks strict JSON syntax and compares configuration keys and types with the bundled schema.

faq.question: Does it install mirrord?
faq.answer: No. It points users to approved installation processes and does not run installers automatically.

faq.question: Can it access my Kubernetes cluster?
faq.answer: No. It cannot confirm live cluster resources, credentials, permissions, or runtime behavior.

faq.question: How should I handle secrets?
faq.answer: Do not paste secret values into prompts. Use narrow environment and filesystem rules, and keep sensitive files out of shared configurations.
